To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the double-differential and the integral cross sections of light charged particles produced in the reactions of 50 MeV3He with 112Sn are measured and the corresponding mechanisms of reactions have been determined using the exciton preequilibrium model.

1) the experimental double differential and integral cross section spectra of the 3He + 112Sn reactions at 50 MeV were measured; 2) the theoretical calculations of the experimental spectra were performed; 3) the reaction mechanism was determined.
the experimental double-differential and the integral spectra of (He, xp), He, xd), He, xt), He, x3He and He, xα reactions on Sn nuclei are presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of nuclear reactions induced by light ions.
the study of light charged particles emitted from a 112Sn target when it is bombarded with 50 MeV alpha particles.
the investigation of the mechanisms of nuclear reactions induced by light charged particles on nuclei with mass number A = 112.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work provides a new and more detailed experimental data on the ejection of particles from the nuclei induced by 3He ions, and also a new and more accurate analysis of these data.
the present work is a good example of a successful application of the exciton model to the description of the preequilibrium processes in the reactions induced by heavy ions.
the experimental results can be useful in the study of nuclear reaction mechanisms and in the development of the theory of nuclear reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have studied the ejection of charged particles induced by light ions upon interacting with heavy target nuclei, which is important for understanding the nuclear reaction mechanisms and for developing the nuclear reaction models.
it has been a success in the sense of the following points.
the experimental results are in good agreement with the theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ejection of charged particles is a complex process, and the ejection of particles with a mass of 3He and α is possible only in the case of a large excitation energy of the residual nucleus.

the ejection of charged particles from nuclei is an effective way to obtain information about the structure of nuclei, as well as the mechanisms of the processes of the interaction of ions of heavy nuclei with nuclei of the target material.
the exciton model can describe the experimental spectra of the reactions.
